Pakistan’s 2021 Cement Export Ban Reshaped Construction Materials Industry

Pakistan’s 2021 temporary ban on cement exports, implemented to ensure domestic supply and curb rising prices, had a significant impact on the nation’s construction materials industry, according to sector analysts and company executives. The embargo, which was in place from March to September 2021, targeted all outbound shipments of cement and clinker—a key component in cement production.

Industry leader Lucky Cement Ltd was among the companies affected by the measure. The ban prompted a sharp decline in export revenues, with estimates from the All Pakistan Cement Manufacturers Association (APCMA) suggesting a 32% year-on-year drop in export volume during the embargo period. “We understood the government’s concerns about local shortages, but the abrupt halt to exports disrupted established trade relationships and created uncertainty for future contracts,” said a spokesperson for Lucky Cement Ltd.

Analysts at Karachi-based brokerage Altan Securities noted that the policy succeeded in stabilizing domestic cement prices, which had surged by as much as 18% in early 2021. However, they added that the embargo reduced foreign exchange earnings for the industry during a period when global demand, particularly from markets in East Africa and Sri Lanka, was robust.

“Aside from short-term revenue losses, the industry faced challenges re-entering some export markets after the ban was lifted,” said APCMA chairman Imran Qureshi. He called for more predictable policy measures in the future, noting, “Frequent disruptions undermine competitiveness and long-term growth for Pakistan’s construction materials sector.”
